newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma announced changes to her health bills on Thursday, including dropping provisions on copyright of medicines and the inclusion of a clause allowing medical students to do community service instead of compulsory extra training.
- The Reserve Bank has taken a swipe at labour and the government in its latest Quarterly Bulletin, saying planned changes to basic employment conditions could be bad for jobs.

- The Reserve Bank has arranged a three-year 1.5 billion dollar revolving credit facility as part of a show of strength to the currency market ahead of the planned easing of exchange controls next month.

- A British defence industry consortium has proposed a gold-based arms deal with South Africa including corvettes and submarines for the navy, jet fighters and trainers for the air force and tanks for the army worth several billions of rands over two decades.
- The decision to reopen trade in ivory was a victory for the principle of sustainable use of natural resources, say delegates to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES).
BUSINESS REPORT

- Sasol Ltd, the petrochemicals-from-coal producer, and South Africa's oil refiners have become embroiled in a legal wrangle over Sasol's entry into gas retailing, said Kevin Mulder, supply and trading manager of Caltex Oil South Africa.

- Sancino (Projects) Ltd, a Western Cape-based black empowerment group, has acquired a 10 percent stake in New Clicks Holdings Ltd for 100 million rand. This follows the unbundling of Malbak Ltd which freed the retail group of a controlling shareholder.

- The Reserve Bank has arranged a $1.5 billion credit facility with a group of international banks to supplement its foreign exchange reserves ahead of next month's easing of exchange controls on private individuals.

- An unexpected drop in exports was the main culprit behind a widening of South Africa's current account deficit to 1.9 billion rand in the first quarter of this year from a thin 100 million rand in the fourth quarter of last year, the Reserve Bank said on Thursday.

- Irvin & Johnson (I&J) Ltd, the fishing and frozen food group, is preparing to move aggressively into the fast growing southeast Asian market through a joint venture with Australian partner Simplot, Roy Gordon, the company's managing director, said on Thursday.
THE STAR

- The big-spending Independent Broadcasting Authority, which has gained a reputation for huge hotel bills and international travel, owes its creditors 3.8 million rand and will approach Parliament for an additional 13 million rand to stay within its budget this year.
- Former Welsh Secretary William Hague, 36, won the leadership of Britain's Conservative Party on Thursday, becoming the party's youngest leader in 200 years.
- The Truth and Reconciliation Commission says it cannot give in to demands by the National Party and has called on the Nats to iron out its difficulties with the commission through dialogue.
- Adriaan Vlok, believed to be the only apartheid minister to have applied for amnesty for his involvement in specific acts of terror, has admitted to various "anti-social acts" in his application.
